artifacts.02_existing_storage_audit.md:
# Existing storage audit

[ParquetStorage.store_daily](support/audited-source/src/omegadata/track_a/storage.py) writes a deterministic day path ending `part-00000.parquet`. The anonymous disposable regression reproduced replacement on repeated day writes: LEGACY_RISK_RETAINED; new store is OPT_IN_REPLACEMENT. The legacy API and expectations remain unchanged.

[ReleaseManager](support/audited-source/src/omegadata/track_b/release_manager.py) has release-directory writers, manifest/release profiles and signing integration: WRAP/FUTURE_OD11. No operational writer or signing path was invoked. API/release-readiness readers consume legacy release paths; integration remains separate. [ClickHouseWarehouseSync](support/audited-source/src/omegadata/track_a/warehouse.py) opens a configured client and writes warehouse data: BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, inspected as code only. Existing Arrow/Pandas/SQLAlchemy schemas and domain conventions were reused. Approved source search covered `src`, scripts and tests only; no payload-root search. Exact audit source hashes and function lines are in support/storage-audit.json.
artifacts.03_storage_architecture_decision.md:
# Storage architecture decision

Use existing PyArrow23.0.1 + immutable Parquet + SQLAlchemy2.0.49/SQLite transactional catalog. Arrow typed scanning covers bounded projection, predicates, scalar aggregation and stable-identity metadata joins without another dependency. DuckDB is absent in the permitted environment; its install/license/version experiment is NOT_RUN_DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE. No dependency or network setting changed.

SQLite commits govern reader visibility, while no-replace file installs and retained orphans make cross-resource failure recoverable. This does not make filesystem and SQLite one atomic resource. UUID identities avoid manifest alias across catalogs; operation input digests provide idempotency within the catalog. Exchange/month partitions and8192-row zstd groups are bounded defaults; measured snappy/zstd and group-size alternatives are retained without asserting universal optimality. See [measurements](21_performance_results.json).
artifacts.04_canonical_schema_registry.md:
# Canonical schema registry

[schema.py](source/src/omegadata/canonical_storage/schema.py) provides immutable physical schema fingerprints for canonical/v1 and/v2. source_observations and adjustment_results use separate RAW/DERIVED Parquet domains. instrument_identity_revisions, listing_lifecycle, session_calendar, corporate_action_revisions, universe_membership_revisions, universe_snapshots, universe_member_decisions, reconciliation_results, anomaly_records, review_revisions, correction_revisions, reprocess_requests and reprocess_completions use typed transactional metadata.

Exact domain/class whitelists prevent a parser object from masquerading as a review revision. One-to-many relationships remain nested typed references and immutable ledger records. Domain rows are not collapsed into one wide financial table. Full Arrow schema/type text and domain map are in support/schema-contract.json. No operational schema migration occurred.
artifacts.05_precision_and_type_contract.md:
# Precision and type contract

UTC microsecond timestamps, date32 dates, int64 positive source ordinals, string IDs retaining leading zeros, nullable fields, bool eligibility and explicit list/struct lineage. Null, missing, unavailable, invalid and genuine zero are separate states.

Raw fixed Decimal128(38,12), factor fixed Decimal256(76,36); values must fit exactly. CALCULATION overflow uses a canonical coefficient string/exponent codec (bounded1,000digits, exponent±9999), never a float or silent rounding. Exact rational terms are separate numerator/positive-denominator strings. Lossless coefficient/exponent retains Decimal trailing-zero quantum; optional fixed columns are independently reconciled on read. Raw unsupported precision refuses. Calculation precision and storage precision are distinct; display formatting is not a financial transform.

Literal Decimal/rational known-answer tests cover boundaries, trailing zeros, negative scalar values where allowed, null/zero, timezone normalization, physical-column tampering and nested lineage. No new market observation was created.
artifacts.06_upstream_admission_contract.md:
# Upstream admission

[admission.py](source/src/omegadata/canonical_storage/admission.py) pins exact parser metadata, OD06 identity/calendar, OD07 proof/context/result, OD08 complete decision snapshots, and OD09 source/comparison/review/reprocess contracts. A ParsedResult receipt never grants financial authority. Authentic parser rows cannot be retained under this code-only capability; metadata-only receipts remain reusable.

Derived volume replays the OD07 bound proof and binds exact consumed value, observation, source row/artifact, security/listing/venue/session, currency/basis and upstream digests. Universe snapshots replay the exact context and preserve excluded/unresolved entries. Reconciliation strict scopes independently select required persisted observations by source/listing/field/session/cutoff; unknown availability refuses and future-known rows cannot enter earlier contexts. Publisher/reported identifier/lineage/financial-field metadata are bound to exact source-observation digests. Tolerance quality stays provisional unless independently authorized.

The final negative test reproduced a metadata payload rights bypass. Recursive bounded admission now refuses denied/non-canary evidence and parser financial rows before any transaction. Caller labels cannot grant real source access. Non-market records always remain financially ineligible.
# Partition and file manifests

Each exchange/month partition has an immutable UUID Parquet object. Entries bind exact relative path, SHA256, byte length, row count, schema fingerprint, partition, dataset version, min/max trade dates and known times, compression/writer and classification. Strict integer checks reject bool counts. Reader independently reconciles these semantics against actual decoded rows and Parquet compression.

Paths are manifest-only, bounded and relative; traversal, unknown names, symlinks, hardlinks, changed bytes and changed descriptor identities refuse. Linux descriptor-anchored `/proc/self/fd` opens preserve the retained Python audit guard without weakening its protected roots. Files are installed O_EXCL with fsync; existing files are never replaced. Unreferenced files cannot join a query through directory globbing. Only approved/generated code-only outputs were hashed.
artifacts.08_dataset_version_contract.md:
# Immutable dataset versions

Dataset/version/schema/partition/file/manifest/operation identities are distinct. Exact sorted input digest binds operation retry; opaque version IDs bind a unique manifest within/across tested catalogs. Same operation plus changed inputs refuses. # Atomic reader-visible commit

Pin definition/rows/operation/parent/expected partition set. Write private attempt files. Decode and reconcile every staged typed value. Install immutable files without replacement. In BEGIN IMMEDIATE, recheck operation identity and expected parent, bind complete file/partition/dependency/manifest metadata and commit catalog. Reopen committed version through the normal verified reader.

Concurrent incompatible successors are refused, not silently last-writer-wins. Installed files before a failed transaction remain orphans. A postcommit/preack retry returns the original operation identity. File fsync and directory fsync support local process-crash recovery; this is not hardware power-loss certification. Supported readers see committed manifests only. [Process results](10_concurrency_verification.json) and [fault evidence](11_crash_recovery_and_orphan_accounting.md) preserve exact tested guarantees.

# Crash recovery and orphans

Seven actual independent-worker terminations were exercised at before_write, during_file_write, after_file_write_before_validation, after_validation_before_install, after_install_before_catalog_commit, during_catalog_transaction and after_catalog_commit_before_acknowledgement. The trusted coordinator killed only its exact spawned process group. Independent readers verified V1 during each paused writer; only the postcatalog checkpoint exposed the new operation. Restart/retry preserved original manifest/rows and never promoted an orphan.

Three independent-process races covered identical same-operation retry, changed content under the same operation, and competing successor operations sharing a parent. Identical retries converged; incompatible writes refused. Each worker retained the namespace/seccomp boundary and only one explicitly owned non-market shared directory was added. Full launches, exits, probes and outcomes are in support/process. Orphan inventory is read-only; no automatic cleanup, deletion, guessing or recovery promotion exists. These are process-kill tests, not disk/power-loss or Windows certification.
artifacts.12_schema_evolution_contract.md:
# Schema evolution

canonical/v2 adds nullable source_note without changing canonical/v1. Physical types plus semantic version metadata have immutable fingerprints. Conversion decodes verified historical bytes and writes a new version, referencing its parent; previous files remain intact. Unknown schemas and unsupported/reverse lossy conversion refuse rather than relying on an Arrow cast.

Increasing precision or changing financial semantics requires a new explicit implementation/version; it is not silently treated as compatible. The bounded current converter is the tested v1→v2 additive path; arbitrary conversions are unsupported. Original and converted query results, restart, old manifest and byte identities were checked on disposable storage.
artifacts.13_metadata_catalog_and_rollback.md:
# Catalog and rollback

Thirteen additive catalog tables cover schema versions, definitions, versions, physical files, partition references, operations, dependencies, selection events, typed references, source indexes, comparison scopes and catalog version. FKs, unique IDs, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, synchronous FULL and immutable UPDATE/DELETE triggers preserve accepted facts. Typed payload codec reuses existing upstream persistence conventions; it is not pickle or arbitrary dynamic module loading.

Read-only consumers use SQLite query_only plus explicit write refusal; opening a reader does not acquire the initialization writer transaction. This is an API/SQL read-only guarantee inside the worker, not protection from arbitrary same-process access to its engine or host admin writes.

Rollback selects the exact old committed manifest with an append-only development event. Empty disposable schema rollback is tested; any nonempty fact/object/manifest refuses destructive rollback. No accepted history is deleted. The catalog is tested in owned disposable file-backed SQLite; upstream in-memory repository regressions remain separately passing. No operational migration was performed.
artifacts.14_dependency_index_contract.md:
# Dependency and reprocess impact

Exact (kind,identity,digest) edges bind source/identity/calendar/action/adjustment/universe/reconciliation/review/correction/reprocess references to storage versions and intermediate metadata. Full-body typed pins include dependencies, so an identical ID cannot silently acquire changed edges. Reverse indexes and bounded transitive queries return all registered matching historical outputs, not only the currently selected version.

Unknown knowledge time is not inferred. Future-known metadata is excluded at the requested cutoff. Later corrections do not invalidate legitimate earlier as-known files. Coverage remains DEPENDENCY_UNKNOWN: registered edges are searchable but missing upstream registration cannot self-certify complete reprocess impact. No repair/recompute job runs automatically. OD11 must combine these exact references with OD09 independently verified completion requirements.
artifacts.15_PIT_query_contract.md:
# Version-pinned analytical queries

Query requires immutable version, dataset, half-open date range, aware known_at, compatible basis/profile and bounded rows/files/date span. Stable listing/security and exchange filters are explicit. Every manifest member is integrity verified before file/partition pruning; selected Parquet fragments read only the verified captured bytes. Predicate filtering cannot reopen a changed path. Projection preserves requested logical fields; exact Fraction aggregation avoids float/ambient Decimal rounding. Stable-ID metadata joins account for unmatched/ambiguous rows and remain unverified.

Unknown version/schema, manifest corruption, incompatible basis/purpose, unsupported projection, missing availability and resource excess produce typed refusal or explicit audit exclusion. AUDIT is the only enabled consumer; neither newest-version nor wall-clock defaults exist. No arbitrary SQL, remote URL, extension, shell or user-supplied filesystem path is exposed. Integrity verification necessarily reads all manifest files; selective scan counts are distinct from files verified.
artifacts.16_arrow_duckdb_evaluation.md:
# Arrow and DuckDB evaluation

Arrow23.0.1 was already permitted and passes exact Decimal/date/timestamp/string/list lineage roundtrip, versioned manifests, stable filters, projection, exact scalar aggregation and metadata joins. The scanner uses Parquet fragments from verified buffers; partition/date pruning chooses only catalog-approved members. Independent literal expected row counts and sums were checked at1k/10k/100k structural scales.

DuckDB is not installed. No unrestricted network/install was enabled, no version/license adoption was claimed, and no DuckDB performance result exists. Therefore retain Arrow. This is a dependency-constrained comparison, not a claim that Arrow outperforms an unexecuted engine. Actual timings, RSS, file sizes, compression alternatives and query-plan evidence are in [performance](21_performance_results.json).
artifacts.17_hard_blocks_and_quarantine.md:
# Hard blocks and quarantine

Financial/publication/execution eligibility are derived non-writable false states in this code-only store. Storage-valid canary serialization is not financial acceptance. Identity/availability/rights/authority/history/coverage/reconciliation/review/reprocess references and block reasons remain explicit; confidence cannot erase them.

Payload commit admits only explicitly non-market structural inputs. Typed upstream persistence additionally rejects denied/non-canary source evidence and parser financial rows. Source-authorized payload admission is deliberately unavailable without a separately reviewed capability. A quarantine label is not permission to copy restricted data. Metadata-only receipts are retained where allowed; no denied or restricted original payload was copied. Authenticated positive-path validation remains blocked.
artifacts.18_negative_first_tests.md:

Frozen initial F01–F28 criteria and actual red/green logs are preserved in support. First run:52failed/1passed, with missing new package and a passing legacy overwrite reproduction. A new init=False test changed its expected exception class to ValueError, and new strict-scope fixture cutoffs were corrected to their actual existing context date; original frozen versions and failures remain available. No historical financial assertion changed.

Subsequent actual failures drove narrow corrections: retry manifest collision; physical scalar/codec mismatch; zero quantum; immutable typed APIs; source scope/index completeness; dependency pin identity; independent manifest semantics; cross-catalog version identity; wrong-domain metadata; reconciliation replay; stable-ID join; lock-free reader initialization; retained Python audit guard compatibility; and final denied-source metadata payload admission.

All106 focused controls passed after the last functional correction. Earlier failed runs, parser/collection syntax incident in a new source append, and initial CRLF-normalizing patch replay failure are retained. The successful final patch is byte-preserving and EOF-aware. Negative-first evidence is engineering evidence, never authentic financial acceptance. See support/negative-chronology.json.
